comparison: Both evaluate the protocol development and validation (C1, C18, C20-C22). OpenEval finds the protocol well-characterized with appropriate molecular validation and rates it SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also accept the protocol's success, with Reviewer 1 acknowledging 'capacity for iPSC Myoblasts to be generated' and Reviewer 2 requesting validation with newer kits but not challenging the methodology itself. Both SUPPORTED.

Both address marker expression and characterization (C23-C24 overlap, plus C2-C3, C28-C29, C33, C43-C44, C50, C64 in peer review). OpenEval finds immunofluorescence data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 specifically requesting protein-level quantification: 'Pax 3 and MyoD not quantified at the protein level' and 'lack of IF quantifications.' Disagreement on sufficiency of evidence.

Both evaluate expansion capacity and stable maintenance (C30-C31, C159). OpenEval finds the proliferation assays and passage experiments SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 noting 'viable primary lines committed to differentiate' and neither reviewer challenging expansion claims. Agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Both address myogenic commitment and differentiation capacity (C32, C34-C35). OpenEval finds flow cytometry and FAC-sorting data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 specifically requesting: 'Fusion stated to be a key difference...but not quantified' and 'Tertiary reserve population experiment not quantified.' Disagreement on whether quantification is sufficient.

Both evaluate scRNA-seq analysis and clustering (C36-C50 in OpenEval; C36-C42, C46-C49, C51-C63 in peer review). OpenEval finds the comprehensive analysis with UMAP clustering and gene expression profiling SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 stating 'Figure 3: conclusion/take home message unclear,' indicating difficulty interpreting the transcriptome analysis despite not challenging data quality. Disagreement on clarity and interpretability.

OpenEval R6 addresses pathway analysis (C51-C64) while peer R5 includes some overlapping claims (C51-C63) within broader transcriptome evaluation. OpenEval finds pathway analysis with edgeR and FDR correction SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate the broader transcriptome section UNCERTAIN due to unclear conclusions, though they don't directly challenge the pathway analysis methodology.

Both evaluate differentiation comparisons (C65-C69 in OpenEval; C65-C76 in peer review). OpenEval finds qPCR data comparing differentiation SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'differentiation of 2 to 7 days...sounds like a rather wide spectrum' and expressing concern about consistency of differentiation timing. Disagreement on whether timing variability affects interpretation.

Both address media supplement effects on differentiation (C70-C76). OpenEval finds NanoString data and microscopy SUPPORTED, though notes mechanistic explanations are inferences. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to concerns about differentiation timing variability (2-7 days), which could affect interpretation of media supplement effects.

Both evaluate DUX4 upregulation in FSHD models (C85-C91 in OpenEval; C85-C99 in peer review). OpenEval finds qPCR and reporter assay data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating the FSHD section is 'overly technical and difficult to digest for non specialists' and requesting clarification of 'actual advance in terms of in vitro FSHD modelling.' Disagreement on clarity and significance rather than data quality.

Both address media effects on DUX4 expression (C92-C98). OpenEval finds NanoString data SUPPORTED, noting mechanistic inferences about corticosteroids are not directly tested. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, finding the FSHD section difficult to interpret and requesting quantification of Dux4 from reporter cell line. Disagreement on sufficiency of presentation and quantification.

Both evaluate DUX4 developmental repression (C99-C103 in OpenEval; C100-C113 in peer review). OpenEval finds the lack of early upregulation SUPPORTED, noting appropriate qualification of findings. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, finding the FSHD section 'overly technical' and requesting clearer presentation of significance, though not directly challenging the methylation data or contradiction with prior studies.

Both address methylation analysis (C104-C108). OpenEval finds bisulfite sequencing data SUPPORTED, noting appropriate explanation of contradiction with prior work. Peer reviewers rate the broader FSHD section UNCERTAIN due to difficulty understanding significance, though they don't specifically challenge the methylation methodology or 4qA-specific primer approach.

Both evaluate MYOD1 methylation as control (C109-C111). OpenEval finds this control experiment SUPPORTED, demonstrating functional methylation machinery. Peer reviewers rate the broader FSHD section UNCERTAIN but don't specifically challenge this control experiment, which strengthens the conclusion about 4qA allele behavior.

Both address 5-AzaC treatment effects (C112-C113). OpenEval finds dose-dependent DUX4 upregulation SUPPORTED, noting the regulatory locus is not identified. Peer reviewers rate the broader FSHD section UNCERTAIN, requesting clearer presentation of advances in FSHD modeling, though not directly challenging the 5-AzaC data.

Both evaluate xenograft engraftment (C114-C123 in OpenEval; C5-C7, C114-C128 in peer review). OpenEval finds immunofluorescence and qPCR data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 requesting 'quantification of LAMIN A/C & SPECTRIN double positive donor derived fibers.' Agreement on successful engraftment but disagreement on sufficiency of quantification.

Both address engraftment efficiency quantification (C124-C128). OpenEval finds NanoString data quantifying human/mouse RNA ratios SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting more rigorous quantification of donor-derived fibers. Disagreement on whether RNA-based quantification is sufficient versus protein-based fiber counting.

Both evaluate MYH isoform switching in xenografts (C129-C135, with C16 in peer review). OpenEval finds 100-fold expression changes SUPPORTED, demonstrating developmental maturation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 noting xenograft properties validate the lineage and Reviewer 2 not challenging the quantitative findings. Agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Both evaluate LGMDR7 disease modeling (C136-C140). OpenEval finds qPCR, immunofluorescence, and cited gene editing SUPPORTED, though notes gene editing data is from prior work. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating 'LGMDR7: this section appears out of context and brief.' Disagreement on sufficiency of presentation and contextual integration.

Both evaluate S1 cell engraftment as negative control (C141-C142). OpenEval finds poor engraftment data SUPPORTED as validation of iMyoblast superiority. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, with neither reviewer challenging this comparative finding. Agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Both evaluate FKRP disease modeling (C143-C150). OpenEval finds immunofluorescence, qPCR, laminin binding, and Western blots SUPPORTED, demonstrating dose-dependent loss of function. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'novelty is limited' and 'reported findings are very limited in terms of disease modelling,' citing prior work. Disagreement on novelty and significance rather than data quality.

Both evaluate regenerative capacity and PAX3+ progenitor maintenance (C151-C156). OpenEval finds immunofluorescence showing PAX3+ nuclei after primary and secondary injury SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting 'serial injuries or transplantation' validation, 'quantification of contribution to satellite cell pool,' and 'quantification of donor derived Pax7+ cells in vivo.' Disagreement on extent of validation required, particularly for PAX7+ cells.

Both address protocol advantages and applicability (C157-C160). OpenEval finds broad applicability and expansion capacity SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 finding the method 'successful and efficient' but Reviewer 2 questioning 'what the key advantage over other methods and over the commercial kit is' and noting 'Pax7 remains low.' Divided assessment on whether advantages are sufficiently demonstrated.

Both discuss advantages of iMyoblasts over alternatives (C161-C163). OpenEval finds discussion points SUPPORTED, noting 3D modeling potential is speculative. Peer reviewers rate the broader advantages section UNCERTAIN, questioning whether iMyoblasts provide sufficient advantages over existing methods and noting the limitation of low PAX7 expression.

Both address overall protocol establishment and therapeutic potential (C184-C185). OpenEval finds summary statements SUPPORTED, noting therapeutic applications are appropriately qualified as speculative. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with divided opinions: Reviewer 1 finds it 'attractive and thorough' while Reviewer 2 questions advantages over existing methods. Disagreement on overall significance.

OpenEval evaluates background claims on DUX4 and FSHD (C77-C84) as SUPPORTED, noting these are knowledge claims with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background/context claims.

OpenEval evaluates iMyoblast identity characterization (C164-C167) as SUPPORTED, synthesizing flow cytometry, scRNA-seq, and developmental trajectory data. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this identity synthesis, though related concerns appear in R2 and R5.

OpenEval evaluates speculative discussion about PAX3+ cell relationships (C168-C170) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these specific mechanistic hypotheses.

OpenEval evaluates regulatory plasticity discussion (C171-C173) as SUPPORTED based on MYH isoform switching data, noting mechanistic speculation is appropriately qualified. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this plasticity discussion.

OpenEval evaluates stem cell characteristics synthesis (C174-C178) as SUPPORTED, noting dual commitment is demonstrated and mechanistic uncertainty is acknowledged. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this stem cell characteristics synthesis.

OpenEval evaluates expansion and maintenance mechanisms discussion (C179-C183) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate acknowledgment of unknown mechanisms and reasonable future directions. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this mechanistic discussion.
